synthesis.paragraph: The paper "How accessibility perception can improve accessibility measurement" shares seven references with the June 12, 2026 paper "Determinants of perceived accessibility of public transport and implications for equity: Evidence, gaps, and a research agenda", including "How Accessibility Shapes Land Use", "Accessible accessibility research challenges", and "Perceived accessibility is an important factor in transport choice — Results from the AVENUE project". Additionally, "How accessibility perception can improve accessibility measurement" shares five references with the July 1, 2026 paper "Operationalizing accessibility thresholds: Identifying perceived minimum and sufficient accessibility in Canada", including "How Accessibility Shapes Land Use", "What about the people? Developing measures of perceived accessibility from case studies in Germany and the UK", and "Perceived accessibility: What it is and why it differs from calculated accessibility measures based on spatial data". Another paper, "Assessing gendered accessibility inequalities to urban facilities among refugees: A 3SFCA method", shares four references with the July 6, 2026 paper "Beyond proximity: Behavioral equity in urban park use in Shanghai", including "Measures of Spatial Accessibility to Health Care in a GIS Environment: Synthesis and a Case Study in the Chicago Region", "A complex landscape of inequity in access to urban parks: A literature review", and "Who has access to urban vegetation? A spatial analysis of distributional green equity in 10 US cities". Over the last 30 days, Tongji University appeared on 31 papers, Hong Kong Polytechnic University appeared on 26 papers, Peking University appeared on 20 papers, and Tsinghua University appeared on 18 papers.
